advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Include `overflow` (and decide about `indeterminate`) in `_surfaced`, or pass a large `advisory_cap` to `review_plan`, so the overlap metric is not distorted by the cap
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:115: found = [*((verdict or {}).get("blocking") or []), *((verdict or {}).get("advisory") or [])]

src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:222-231: review_plan(...) is called without advisory_cap, so the default cap applies
engine_comparison_results.json: several items record exactly 19 pipeline findings ("pipeline_only": 19), which suggests the list was truncated at the cap
advisory.finding: The finding-overlap metric only sees each verdict's cap-truncated `advisory` list. The default advisory cap of 20 truncates advisories before overlap is computed, and `overflow` (plus `indeterminate`) is never read. The pipeline sorts advisories by priority before the cap, while agentic findings keep the agent's order. So the recorded pipeline-only/agentic-only counts are partly an artifact of the cap, and findings past the cap that would have matched are never compared.
scenarios: The pipeline produces 30 advisories. Only the top 20 by priority are compared, so an agentic finding that matches advisory #25 counts as agentic-only.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_surfaced`, also collect `verdict.get("overflow")` (and optionally `indeterminate`), or call `review_plan(..., advisory_cap=10**6)` in `_review_once` so every finding reaches the comparison.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Refuse to resume (or drop the resume state) when the saved `corpus_digest`/`match_threshold` differ from the current run
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:344-348: done = {i["review_event_uuid"]: i for i in (resume or {}).get("items", []) if all(i[e]["outcome"] != "error" for e in ENGINES)}

src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:370: "corpus_digest": corpus_digest(labels_path, rows), is recomputed fresh and never compared with resume["corpus_digest"]
advisory.finding: `--resume` reuses saved items from the `--out` file without checking that its `corpus_digest`, `corpus` or `match_threshold` match the current run. If the labels file, `--limit` or the threshold changed, stale per-item records (including `overlap` computed under the old threshold) are mixed into the new summary, and the rewritten file carries the new digest.
scenarios: An operator regenerates the labels file (new content hash) and reruns with `--resume` against the old results path. Matching uuids are reused, and the output claims the new digest.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `run` (or `main`), when `resume` is given and `resume.get("corpus_digest") != corpus_digest(labels_path, rows)` or `resume.get("match_threshold") != MATCH_THRESHOLD`, raise SystemExit with a clear message instead of reusing the items.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_default_labels` fail (or require `--labels`) when more than one `labels-*.jsonl` exists instead of choosing by hash order
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:385: found = sorted(replay_dir().glob("labels-*.jsonl"))
src/rebar/llm/evals/engine_comparison.py:388: return found[0]

advisory.finding: `_default_labels` picks `sorted(glob('labels-*.jsonl'))[0]`. The files are named by content hash, so when the replay dir holds more than one labels file this picks the lexicographically smallest hash. That is an arbitrary file, not the newest or the frozen one, and nothing reports that other files were ignored.
scenarios: After plan_replay writes a second labels file, a default run silently compares a different corpus than the recorded one.
advisory.suggested_fix: If `len(found) > 1`, raise SystemExit listing the candidates and asking for `--labels`.

advisory.finding: No end-to-end test checks the finding-overlap numbers, one of the harness's main reported results. In every run test the pipeline returns no findings, and the one agentic finding produced (row 3 of the first run test) is never checked in the item's findings list or overlap. Pulling findings out of a real review verdict (`_surfaced`) and matching them inside `review_row` is only tested with hand-built dicts and hand-built item records. If `_surfaced` read the wrong field of a real verdict, or `review_row` passed the wrong lists to `match_findings`, every recorded overlap would silently become 0/0/0 and all tests would still pass.
scenarios: The real verdict's surfaced-finding key changes, or `_surfaced` is edited to read `title`. Every surfaced list becomes empty strings or empty lists, overlap collapses, and no test fails.
`review_row` swaps or drops a findings list when calling `match_findings`. pipeline_only and agentic_only come out wrong in the committed results file, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_identical_verdicts_agree_and_a_blocker_flips, also assert `results["items"][2]["agentic"]["findings"]` contains 'the plan names the wrong module' and `results["items"][2]["overlap"]["agentic_only"] == 1`. Then add a run where `_Scripted` also returns a near-identical finding from a pipeline Pass-1 contract, and assert `summary["overlap"]["matched"] == 1`.
